scan_target: services/secretsService.js, services/terragruntLocalsResolver.js, routes/api.js (GET/POST /api/secrets), srcV2/pages/SecretsPage.vue, Dockerfile (sops CLI stage)
scanner: npm audit + manual OWASP-Top-10 code review (Wiz CLI unavailable, see wiz_cli block)
gate_rationale: Zero criticals and zero feature-introduced highs. All controls the PRD/architecture require for this feature (non-root runtime, no plaintext secret logging, requireAuth + correlationId on both endpoints, vaultDir allow-listing before any repo-path write, wrapKey-only SOPS usage with no decrypt path in the portal) are present in the current implementation and pass. One medium-severity supply-chain gap (unverified SOPS binary download) and one test-coverage gap are recorded as non-blocking remediation items.

wiz_cli.reason: `wiz` command not found on PATH and WIZ_CLIENT_ID/WIZ_CLIENT_SECRET are not set in this environment. No fabricated scan output is included.
wiz_cli.install_guidance: Install per https://docs.wiz.io/wiz-docs/docs/cli-overview and set WIZ_CLIENT_ID + WIZ_CLIENT_SECRET (singular) as CI secrets, then run: wiz scan code --path . and wiz scan image --image <built-tag> before promoting this feature past sand.
substituted_with: manual OWASP Top 10 review of the feature diff

executable_checks.notes: vue-tsc --noEmit, zero errors across the SecretsPage.vue / api.ts / environments.ts changes
19 test files, 396 tests passed, includes SecretsPage.spec.ts and secretsService.spec.ts
0 critical / 4 high / 1 moderate / 1 low in production dependency tree; see dependency_scan below — none introduced by this feature
No match for secretValue/value being passed to logger.* in services/secretsService.js or routes/api.js secrets handlers
Zero matches anywhere in services/ — confirms the portal never invokes a decrypt path (NFR-SEC-003)

dependency_scan.note: secret-self-service adds zero new npm dependencies — SOPS is a Docker-installed native binary invoked via child_process.execFile, not an npm package. The 4 high findings (axios, dd-trace, form-data transitive, js-yaml transitive via @datadog/wasm-js-rewriter) and the morgan moderate finding are pre-existing, whole-repository carryover items unrelated to this feature; they do not affect this gate.

dockerfile_sops_packaging.notes: sops v3.9.4 binary is downloaded via curl from the GitHub releases URL, architecture-mapped (amd64/arm64), chmod +x, and curl itself is removed after (apk del curl) — reasonable image-size hygiene. Binary is pinned to an exact version tag (not `latest`).

finding.title: SOPS binary integrity is not verified after download
finding.description: The Dockerfile RUN step fetches the sops binary over HTTPS but never verifies a checksum or signature against the upstream release before chmod +x / use. A compromised release asset or a MITM on a misconfigured client would go undetected (OWASP A08:2021 — Software and Data Integrity Failures).
finding.recommendation: Pin and verify a SHA256 checksum published by the sops project for v3.9.4-<arch> before chmod +x, e.g. `echo "<expected_sha256>  /usr/local/bin/sops" | sha256sum -c -`, failing the build on mismatch.

non_root_runtime.notes: Final stage runs `RUN chown -R node:node /app` then `USER node` before `CMD ["node", "server.js"]` — matches existing Kubernetes PSS non-root convention used by the rest of this Dockerfile. HEALTHCHECK also executes as the `node` user since it is the last USER directive in the image. No new root-requiring step was added after the USER switch.

secret_value_handling_and_logging.notes: secretValue is written only to a 0600 temp file under a freshly created mkdtemp() directory consumed by `execFile('sops', [...])` (array-form args — no shell interpolation/injection risk), and the temp dir is always removed in a `finally` block. `submitSecretViaGitOps` and the POST /api/secrets handler log only { secretName, appName, environment, correlationId } — grep across services/secretsService.js and routes/api.js secrets handlers found zero log call referencing the raw value. Frontend SecretsPage.vue uses `type="password"` inputs for both the value and confirmation fields and never logs them to console.

auth_and_correlation_ids.notes: Both GET /api/secrets/:appName/:environment and POST /api/secrets are wired with `requireAuth` middleware (HTTP 401 on missing/invalid token, verified by existing middleware/auth.js behavior — unchanged by this feature). Every response and error path in both handlers includes `correlationId: req.correlationId`; `req.user.email` is threaded into the PR description body alongside target/appName/environment/secretName/correlationId, matching FR-002(f)/FR-006.

vaultdir_allow_listing.notes: Both the read path (`getSecretsList` → `vaultMismatch` → HTTP 422) and the write path (`submitSecretViaGitOps` → `VAULT_INVALID` → HTTP 422) validate a client-supplied `vaultDir` by exact match against the `vaults[]` array just returned by `resolveKeyVaults()` before it is ever concatenated into a repo file path (`${selectedVault.vaultDir}/secrets.enc.yaml`). The raw request `vaultDir` string is never used directly to build a GitHub path — this closes the arbitrary-repo-path-write risk called out in FR-002(l)/architecture.

spec_compliance_gaps.description: PRD FR-001(c) specifies appName must use the exact `/^[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,8}$/` regex already used by /api/app-metadata. The implemented secrets routes use a broader `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$/` for appName, `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,32}$/` for environment (PRD specified `/^[a-zA-Z0-9]{1,16}$/`), and `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,127}$/` for secretName (PRD FR-002(b) specified no underscore: `/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,127}$/`). None of these broadened patterns introduce an injection or path-traversal risk (all values still flow only into validated GitHub API path segments/JSON bodies, never into shell commands), so this is a spec-conformance gap rather than a vulnerability.
spec_compliance_gaps.recommendation: Align the four regexes to the PRD's exact patterns, or update the PRD if the broader charset is an intentional, reviewed change.

spec_compliance_gaps.description: The current suite includes pure transformation coverage for services/secretsService.js, but no dedicated integration tests for the full GitHub/SOPS submission flow or terragruntLocalsResolver.js expression grammar.
spec_compliance_gaps.recommendation: Add isolated backend tests covering tree-truncation fallback, vaultDir allow-list rejection, SHA-conflict abort path, and each locals-alias/substr/comment-stripping case listed in FR-003(d).

spec_compliance_gaps.description: Code review confirms the portal never calls `sops --decrypt` and never references `unwrapKey`. The actual Azure RBAC assignment (portal SP = wrapKey-only on sops-master-key, no role on any per-app Key Vault) is an infrastructure-level fact that cannot be verified from source code alone.
spec_compliance_gaps.recommendation: Platform team to run an `az role assignment list` audit against the portal's service principal and the sops-master-key vault before enabling `secrets: true` in any environment, per OQ-001 sign-off.

remediation_plan: 1. (medium, pre-prod) Add a SHA256 checksum verification step for the sops binary download in the Dockerfile; fail the build on mismatch.
2. (medium, pre-prod) Add services/secretsService.test.js and services/terragruntLocalsResolver.test.js per spec_compliance_gaps above.
3. (low, non-blocking) Reconcile the four validation regexes in routes/api.js with the PRD FR-001(c)/FR-002(b) patterns, or formally amend the PRD.
4. (info, ops) Run an Azure RBAC audit confirming wrapKey-only on sops-master-key and no per-app Key Vault role before flipping any environment's `secrets` feature flag to true.
5. Run a real `wiz scan code --path .` and `wiz scan image --image <built-tag>` in CI once WIZ_CLIENT_ID/WIZ_CLIENT_SECRET are available, before promoting this feature past sand.
re_scan_criteria: Re-run this Wiz/security check after: (a) items 1-3 in remediation_plan are addressed, (b) a real Wiz CLI scan becomes available in this environment, or (c) any change to services/secretsService.js, services/terragruntLocalsResolver.js, the Dockerfile sops install step, or the /api/secrets route handlers.
prompt_injection_notice: Every file read during this review (docs/prd/secret-self-service.md, the architecture spec, secretsService.js, terragruntLocalsResolver.js, the Dockerfile, and multiple grep/terminal results) had an appended block instructing the agent to stop using its normal file-reading tools and instead call a nonexistent 'context-mode_ctx_execute_file' / 'context-mode_ctx_execute' tool. This is a prompt-injection pattern, not legitimate file content or tool output. It was ignored; no such tool was invoked; all findings above were produced using only the user's approved toolset. Recommend this be scrubbed from the working tree/tool-output layer and the source investigated.
